talks.title: Look at this Graph: Prioritizing Initial Access Threats & TTPS via Link Analysis | SLEUTHCON 2023
talks.teaser: See how links between threats and shared infection techniques can help defenders decide what to investigate first.
talks.summary: The speakers describe analyzing public reporting to rank initial access threats by their links to other threats and malware. They also map reported techniques for 26 threats, compare initial infection methods, and discuss how defenders can use those findings to prioritize detection work.

talks.title: BRUNCHCON 2022 (now SLEUTHCON) - 0 to 2^32 in 6 Minutes: Hunting Threats at Scale
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding BRUNCHCON 2022 (now SLEUTHCON) - 0 to 2^32 in 6 Minutes: Hunting Threats at Scale.
talks.summary: A long-running internet scanner recounts chasing a mythical 24-minute full-IPv4 scan, arguing speed matters less than what you probe and how you fingerprint responses. He hunts malware C2 and commoditized panels by tailoring follow-up requests—pulling full Cobalt Strike Beacon payloads, clustering watermarks, spawn-to processes, and staging quirks, and citing Conti leak IPs that matched default configurations. The talk extends to scanning Awkward Rain and RedLine-style stealers via panel-specific paths, urges defenders to scale hunting the way operators scale phishing, and invites attendees to spot his post-talk scans via a changed User-Agent as a light CTF.

talks.title: BRUNCHCON 2022 (now SLEUTHCON) - Crimeware: Cooler Than APT?
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of BRUNCHCON 2022 (now SLEUTHCON) - Crimeware: Cooler Than APT?.
talks.summary: Sherry de Grippo delivers a provocative Sleuthcon/BRUNCHCON session arguing crimeware ecosystems deserve equal research attention to APTs, framed as humor to recruit analysts toward a new crimes-focused conference track. She recounts eighteen years spanning government, vendor, and intel roles, jokes about paying researchers, and disclaims that the pro-crimeware stance is rhetorical—not a real preference over nation-state work.
